intro:
Approach to Wilno

April 15th, 1919

There is no front here - a railway, four towns on it, nobody in between. Every division that could hold this ground is in the Ukraine or on the Don.

Pilsudski is not trying to break the screen but to get behind it, and Moscow will spend nothing on Wilno: the group is not to be encircled, and the road south stays open until the city Soviet and the rolling stock are out. Hold Olita, Orany and Lida to the last turn.

briliant.text:
The road south is open and the towns on it are still ours at the last hour, which is what I was told to deliver.

I will not dress it up beyond that. Wilno itself will not be held - their cavalry is already north of us and the city has one battalion and a printing press in it. But the Western Division comes out as a division, the Soviet workers of the city have had four days to leave, and the trains went south loaded instead of being taken on the sidings.

The Polish papers will call this the liberation of a Polish city. Two thirds of the countryside around it speaks Byelorussian and will find out this summer what liberation means when the estates come back with the army.

They were across the road before the rearguard reached it. The detachment came out in pieces, on foot, by whatever tracks it could find, and left the depot at Lida burning because there was no time to load it.

The Wilno group has effectively ceased to exist as a formation. What is left of it will be reorganised at Molodeczno, and the units that took Wilno now have an open road to the east for as long as it takes us to build another line.

intro:
Assault on Wilno

April 18th, 1919

They came in at first light along the railway - an armoured train and a cavalry group that rode through the gap to Lida in the dark and were in the streets before the garrison knew the line was cut.

The city is going; that was decided at Olita three days ago. What is not decided is the twelve thousand men and four hospital trains north and east of it, and the city Soviet. Hold Malaty, Swieciany and Wilno until they are through.

briliant.text:
The roads stayed open and the column is through. Rearguard, hospital trains, the Soviet's people and about nine hundred railwaymen who would not have lasted a week in the city.

Wilno is theirs. In the three days after they took it their soldiery went through the Jewish quarter and killed something over sixty people, and their own commission will later put the number lower and call the rest bandits. Remember the number.

We are ordered back to the Berezina line. This is not the end of the business - it is the beginning of a year in which we shall be doing this on ground of their choosing.

The northern road was cut at Swieciany and the eastern one an hour later. What was in the city stayed in the city.

I have no complete return of losses and I will not have one; the men who could get out did so in small parties across country. The Western Front has no reserve to give me and the campaign, as an operation of ours, is over.

intro:
Minsk and the Berezina

August 4th, 1919

The Western Front has sixteen thousand bayonets on four hundred versts and orders that begin with the word nevertheless. Everything that can march is committed against Denikin and Kolchak.

Pilsudski takes Minsk now because Denikin has told Paris that a Polish state is a temporary administrative inconvenience - so Warsaw has a short season in which our defeat is not yet their defeat. The city cannot be held; the Berezina line behind it can. Hold Minsk, Stolpce and the crossings until the 16th Army is on that line.

briliant.text:
The junctions held long enough and the 16th Army is on the Berezina with its guns, its wounded and its staff. Minsk was given up on order, in daylight, with the last train out before the demolition party fired the water tower.

The front now runs where it will run all winter. That is not a victory and I have not written it up as one; it is the difference between a defeated army and a destroyed one, and this autumn there is nothing behind us to replace a destroyed one with.

Their proclamation to the inhabitants of the former Grand Duchy is already posted in Minsk. It promises self-determination. The estates it does not mention are being handed back this week.

The Stolpce crossing went first and the whole line unhinged from it. The 16th Army is across the Berezina in the sense that its men are on the eastern bank; its artillery is not, and neither is a third of its transport.

Byelorussia is lost as far as the river and there is no formation west of it that answers to us any more.

intro:
Dyneburg: the Latgale winter

January 3rd, 1920

Minus twenty-five, snow to the waist off the roads, and not a machine on either side that starts without a fire under it. The 15th Army has been in these positions since November.

The Polish attack, with the Latvian army from the north-west, is political before it is military: put Latgale in Riga's hands and cut the wire between us and Kaunas. The town will be given up if it must be; the corps may not. Hold Dyneburg and the positions covering the crossing to the hour.

briliant.text:
The positions held to the last hour and the corps came out along the ice road with everything that could be pulled.

Dyneburg is Latvian now, which was the point of the whole affair; Warsaw handed the town to Riga within the month and got a treaty for it. Our men walked out of a fortified line in January without breaking, which is a harder thing than it reads.

The Latvians will make peace with us in the spring - they have what they wanted and no appetite for Pilsudski's larger idea. That leaves one enemy on this front instead of two, and it is the only good news in the report.

The line broke at Gajoks in the dark and the crossing was under fire before the hospitals were clear. We left the heavy batteries; there was no moving them once the horses went.

The 15th Army has lost the best part of two divisions to cold and capture, and the north-eastern flank of the front is open all the way to Polotsk.

intro:
Zhitomir: the Polish blow

April 25th, 1920

Three Polish armies and Petliura's two divisions came through the 12th and 14th this morning on a hundred-verst frontage. The 12th is coming apart into detachments.

The object is not Kiev but a Ukrainian state under Petliura, bought last week with eastern Galicia and western Volhynia - four million Ukrainians sold to hire an army, and the villages know it. In six weeks that will be why it fails. Until then hold the Korosten-Zhitomir-Kazatin triangle.

briliant.text:
Five of the six were still ours when the relief came up, and the 12th Army is behind the river instead of in their bag.

They will have Kiev inside a fortnight; that was settled by the frontage, not by this battle. What was settled here is that they will have it with our field armies intact in front of them and a rail net they have to repair before they can use it.

The First Cavalry Army is on the march from the Caucasus. Fourteen thousand sabres, and they are coming the whole way on their own horses.

lose.text:
The triangle went in three days. Korosten first, and after Korosten there was no lateral railway left and the two armies were fighting separate wars a hundred versts apart.

The 12th Army has lost its artillery park and most of a rifle division taken whole. There is no organised force between here and the Dnieper crossings.

intro:
The Dnieper crossings

May 5th, 1920

The order is to give up Kiev without fighting for it, and it is the right order: the city is a salient with a river at its back and their cavalry already north of it at Chernobyl.

A garrison left in it would be a garrison lost, and the 12th Army is worth more than the honour of the streets. The rearguard has the demolition parties, the mined roads and the wire, and almost nothing that moves. Hold the Dnieper crossings until the last battery is over.

briliant.text:
The army is over. Guns, trains, the wounded, the Kiev arsenal's machine tools on flatcars, and the last of the bridge guard on the last span before it went into the river.

They entered the city on the seventh and found the administration gone, the bridges down and no enemy to defeat. Petliura's people expected a rising in their favour; what they got was a population that has seen four armies in three years and has stopped coming out to meet any of them.

Their front is now four hundred versts from its railheads, holding a river line with cavalry it does not have. Ours is on the far bank with the Konarmia marching towards it.

They were on the crossing before the tail of the column. The pontoons went with the engineers still on them and what was left on the western bank had to break up and go north through the marshes in small parties.

The 12th Army has lost its bridging train, its heavy artillery and any claim to be a formation. There will be no counteroffensive from this front for a long time.

intro:
The Red tide

June 4th, 1920

The Konarmia is up: fourteen thousand sabres that walked from the Kuban to the Dnieper in fifty-three days. Tomorrow they go into the seam between the Polish 3rd and 6th Armies at Samhorodok.

Their whole position rests on a front too long for the men holding it, in a country their own requisition parties have turned against them. Break the crust and there is nothing behind it but staffs and depots. Take Zhitomir, Korosten, Fastov and Kazatin - their army cannot withdraw in order without them.

briliant.text:
Every junction on the list is ours and their 3rd Army came out of Kiev on the roads with our cavalry on both sides of it.

At Zhitomir the corps depot went up, five thousand of our people came out of the gaol, and the telegraph office was taken with the operators still at the keys - which is why their army group commander spent two days issuing orders to units that no longer had a line to hear them on.

Kiev is ours again on the twelfth. From here the Southwestern Front goes for Lvov and the Western Front for Warsaw, and there begins the argument that will cost us the campaign.

lose.text:
The breakthrough was made and then not exploited. They got their rearguards onto the junctions ahead of us, ran their trains out, and pulled back to the Sluch in order.

We hold the ground and they keep their army, which is the wrong way round. This front will not get another chance like the fifth of June.

intro:
Before Warsaw: the Wkra

August 13th, 1920

The 1st Cavalry Army was sent for Lvov and has twice been told to come north without coming, and there is a gap of a hundred and fifty versts between the halves of our own front.

The Polish workers who were to rise have volunteered by the hundred thousand instead: an army crossing the Vistula looks less like a revolution than like Russia. The task is not the capital but that this army group is not bagged - hold Ciechanow, Pultusk and Nasielsk, and bring the divisional cores out east.

briliant.text:
The task set me is done. The cores are out east of the Bug with their staffs and their colours, the trains went before them, and the line north of the city held long enough that nothing of mine was cut off in it.

The operation as a whole has failed and I will not write it up otherwise. The counterblow from the Wieprz went in on the sixteenth into a hundred and fifty versts of nothing and rolled up the whole southern half of the front; four divisions of the 4th Army, out of touch with everyone including each other, crossed into East Prussia and were interned. That was decided in July, by the decision to run two offensives on divergent axes with one army's worth of supply, and it was not decided here.

What was decided here is how many of us came back. We are to cover the withdrawal to the Niemen.

The Wkra line went and with it the eastern road. What could not get out is in the encirclement between Nasielsk and the river, and I have no returns from it and expect none.

There is no army group on this front any more, only its remnants, and Warsaw is dictating terms to a front that cannot refuse them. My command is at an end.

intro:
Komarow: the Konarmia breaks out

August 31st, 1920

The Konarmia turned north on the twentieth with Warsaw already lost, and has spent the week riding into a pocket that closed behind it. The Polish 1st Cavalry Division is astride the eastern road at Komarow.

So the last great cavalry battle of this war is fought over a road junction, because everything else is decided. Twelve regiments against six, in fog, at the sabre - and the arithmetic does not help, because they only have to stand. Break out east past Komarow and keep the army.

briliant.text:
We are through. The divisions are east of Komarow, the transport went out ahead of them, and the army that was supposed to be destroyed here is on the Bug in the morning.

It cost us the horses. Whole squadrons came out leading them and a cavalry army without remounts is a rifle division that eats more; the Konarmia will not fight another action like this one, and by October it will be marching south against Wrangel instead, which is where it should have gone in June.

The Poles are calling Komarow their victory and by the ground they are right. But the First Cavalry Army came out of the pocket, and pockets are supposed to keep what goes into them.

intro:
The Niemen

September 20th, 1920

Six weeks ago this army was at the gates of Warsaw. It is digging on the Niemen now with eight thousand rifles where it had thirty, and the conference at Riga has opened.

The line where the war stops will be roughly the line the armies stand on, so every verst held into October is a verst at the table - and Warsaw attacks now precisely because the Entente is about to impose an armistice. Hold Grodno, Lida and the Niemen crossings to the last turn.

briliant.text:
The line is where it was on the twentieth. They came through Lithuania as expected, arrived at Lida a day late and found a division waiting on the ground they meant to arrive behind.

Riga has the news within the day and it is worth more there than here. The delegation reports that the map on the table stopped moving this week.

The Lithuanians have protested the violation of their territory to the League and will be answered with a mutiny that nobody in Warsaw will admit ordering. Their turn comes in three weeks.

lose.text:
Grodno was turned from the north and the whole line came off the river with it. We are back on the Molodeczno road and the delegation at Riga has been told to expect worse terms than it was offered a week ago.

The army I brought out of Poland has been used up covering the ground I was told to hold.

intro:
Back to Minsk

October 9th, 1920

The preliminary peace was signed at Riga three days ago and the guns stop on the eighteenth. This morning Zeligowski's division mutinied, on orders nobody in Warsaw will put in writing, and took Wilno from the Lithuanians.

Both sides are doing the same arithmetic: whatever is held on the eighteenth is what the frontier commission draws its line around next spring. So the front goes forward once more - not for Minsk, already behind our line, but for Molodeczno, Radoszkowicze and the junctions west of it.

briliant.text:
The junctions are ours and the guns stopped with our people standing on them.

The treaty that follows in March gives Poland western Byelorussia and western Volhynia, and gives us the rest of Byelorussia, the Ukraine and six years without a war in the west. It is not a good peace. It is a peace the Republic could not have got in August, when it was being offered the Curzon line and turned it down because it thought it was about to take Warsaw.

Petliura's people are interned. Balakhovich's are still in the marshes and will be cleared out by December. The Konarmia went south a month ago and Wrangel is finished in the Crimea by November.

That is the end of it. Twenty months, from a screen in the Lithuanian forests to a frontier post outside Minsk, and the frontier post is the victory - not because we wanted this line, but because the Republic is still standing behind it. The campaign is over.
